text: King David was now old, advanced in years, and though they covered him with clothes, he could not get warm.

versions.text: King David was now old, advanced in years, and though they covered him with blankets, he could not get warm.
versions.explanation: בְּגָדִים means garments or clothes, not blankets. "Clothes" (or "bedclothes") stays closer to the Hebrew while reading just as smoothly.

text: So his servants said to him, "Let a search be made for a young virgin for my lord the king. Let her attend the king and care for him; let her lie in your arms, and my lord the king will be warm."
They searched throughout the territory of Israel for a beautiful young woman, and they found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.
The young woman was very beautiful. She cared for the king and served him, but the king did not have relations with her.
Now Adonijah son of Haggith put himself forward, saying, "I will be king." He provided himself with chariots and horsemen and fifty men to run ahead of him.
His father had never rebuked him or asked, "Why have you done this?" He was also very handsome, and he was born next after Absalom.
He conferred with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they gave their support to Adonijah.
But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David's own warriors did not side with Adonijah.

Adonijah sacrificed sheep, cattle, and fattened calves at the Stone of Zoheleth, which is beside En Rogel. He invited all his brothers, the king's sons, and all the men of Judah who were royal officials,
but he did not invite Nathan the prophet, or Benaiah, or the warriors, or his brother Solomon.
Then Nathan said to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, "Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, and our lord David knows nothing about it?
Come now, let me advise you how to save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.
Go in to King David and say to him, 'My lord the king, did you not swear to your servant, "Solomon your son shall be king after me, and he shall sit on my throne"? Why then has Adonijah become king?'
While you are still speaking with the king, I will come in after you and confirm what you have said."
So Bathsheba went in to the king in his chamber. The king was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was attending him.
Bathsheba bowed low and paid homage to the king. "What do you want?" the king asked.

versions.text: Bathsheba bowed low and knelt before the king. "What do you want?" the king asked.
versions.explanation: The two Hebrew verbs move from bowing the head (וַתִּקֹּד) to full prostration/homage (וַתִּשְׁתַּחוּ). "Knelt" after "bowed low" reverses the intensification; "paid homage" preserves the progression.

text: She said to him, "My lord, you yourself swore to your servant by the LORD your God: 'Solomon your son shall be king after me, and he shall sit on my throne.'
But now Adonijah has become king, and you, my lord the king, know nothing about it.

He has sacrificed great numbers of cattle, fattened calves, and sheep, and has invited all the king's sons, Abiathar the priest, and Joab the commander of the army, but he has not invited your servant Solomon.
My lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are on you, waiting for you to tell them who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.
Otherwise, as soon as my lord the king rests with his fathers, I and my son Solomon will be treated as criminals."
While she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet arrived.
They told the king, "Nathan the prophet is here." So he came before the king and bowed with his face to the ground.
Nathan said, "My lord the king, have you declared that Adonijah shall be king after you and shall sit on your throne?

For today he has gone down and sacrificed great numbers of cattle, fattened calves, and sheep. He has invited all the king's sons, the commanders of the army, and Abiathar the priest, and right now they are eating and drinking in his presence and shouting, 'Long live King Adonijah!'

versions.text: For today he has gone down and sacrificed great numbers of cattle, fattened calves, and sheep. He has invited all the king's sons, the commanders of the army, and Abiathar the priest, and right now they are eating and drinking with him and shouting, 'Long live King Adonijah!'
versions.explanation: לְפָנָיו means "before him / in his presence," which conveys Adonijah's already-royal posture at the feast; "with him" flattens that nuance.

text: But he did not invite me, your servant, or Zadok the priest, or Benaiah son of Jehoiada, or your servant Solomon.

versions.text: But me, your servant, and Zadok the priest, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and your servant Solomon he did not invite.
versions.explanation: The current word order leaves a long string of objects hanging before the verb, which is hard to follow when read aloud. Fronting the verb keeps the sense and improves oral flow.

text: Has this been done by my lord the king without letting your servant know who is to sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?"

versions.text: Has this been done by my lord the king without letting your servants know who is to sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?"
versions.explanation: The read tradition (Qere) has the singular "your servant," matching Nathan's self-reference in verse 26. The singular is the standard reading.

text: Then King David said, "Call Bathsheba in to me." She came into the king's presence and stood before him.
And the king swore an oath: "As surely as the LORD lives, who has delivered me out of every trouble,
I will carry out this very day what I swore to you by the LORD, the God of Israel: Solomon your son shall be king after me, and he shall sit on my throne in my place."
Then Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground, knelt before the king, and said, "May my lord King David live forever!"
King David said, "Call in Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada." When they came before the king,
he said to them, "Take your lord's servants with you, set my son Solomon on my own mule, and escort him down to Gihon.

versions.text: he said to them, "Take my servants with you, set my son Solomon on my own mule, and escort him down to Gihon.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has David speak of himself in the third person, "the servants of your lord," which is part of the courtly idiom; rendering it "my servants" loses that and departs from the text unnecessarily.

text: There Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet are to anoint him king over Israel. Then blow the trumpet and shout, 'Long live King Solomon!'
Then come back up after him, and let him come and sit on my throne and reign in my place. I have appointed him ruler over Israel and Judah."

versions.text: Then come back up with him, and let him come and sit on my throne and reign in my place. I have appointed him ruler over Israel and Judah."
versions.explanation: אַחֲרָיו means "after him," picturing Solomon leading the procession back up; "with him" obscures this detail of the coronation march.

text: Benaiah son of Jehoiada answered the king, "Amen! May the LORD, the God of my lord the king, so declare it.
As the LORD was with my lord the king, so may he be with Solomon, and may he make his throne even greater than the throne of my lord King David."
So Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Kerethites and the Pelethites went down, set Solomon on King David's mule, and brought him to Gihon.
Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon. Then they sounded the trumpet, and all the people shouted, "Long live King Solomon!"
And all the people went up after him, playing flutes and rejoicing with such great joy that the earth resounded with their noise.

versions.text: And all the people went up after him, playing flutes and rejoicing with such great joy that the ground shook with the sound.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew idiom ("the earth was split by their sound") stresses the deafening volume of the crowd's own voices; "the ground shook with the sound" loses the possessive "their" and slightly weakens the image. "Resounded with their noise" keeps the oral punch of the line.

text: Adonijah and all his guests heard it just as they were finishing their feast. When Joab heard the sound of the trumpet, he said, "Why is the city in such an uproar?"
Even as he spoke, Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest arrived. Adonijah said, "Come in. You are a man of standing; surely you bring good news."
"Not at all," Jonathan answered. "Our lord King David has made Solomon king.
The king sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Kerethites and the Pelethites, and they set him on the king's mule.
Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed him king at Gihon. They came up from there rejoicing, and the city rang with it. That is the noise you heard.

versions.text: Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed him king at Gihon, and they came up from there rejoicing, and the city is in an uproar. That is the noise you heard.
versions.explanation: The verse mixes past narration ("anointed... came up") with a present-tense clause ("the city is in an uproar"), which jars when read aloud. Both Hebrew verbs are narrative past; keeping the tense consistent also avoids the repetition with "uproar" in verse 41.

text: What is more, Solomon has taken his seat on the royal throne.

And the king's servants have come to congratulate our lord King David, saying, 'May your God make Solomon's name greater than yours, and his throne greater than yours!' And the king bowed in worship on his bed.
The king also said, 'Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who has today granted one to sit on my throne while my own eyes look on.'"
At this all Adonijah's guests rose in alarm, and each went his own way.

versions.text: At this all Adonijah's guests rose in alarm and scattered, each going his own way.
versions.explanation: "Scattered" is an added verb not present in the Hebrew, which has only "they arose... and each went his own way." Removing it keeps the content exact and the sentence cleaner for reading aloud.

text: But Adonijah, in fear of Solomon, got up and went and took hold of the horns of the altar.
Then Solomon was told, "Adonijah is afraid of King Solomon and has taken hold of the horns of the altar. He says, 'Let King Solomon swear to me today that he will not put his servant to the sword.'"
Solomon replied, "If he proves himself a man of honor, not a hair of his head will fall to the ground; but if evil is found in him, he will die."
Then King Solomon sent men, and they brought him down from the altar. Adonijah came and bowed before King Solomon, and Solomon said to him, "Go to your house."
